items.content_excerpt: $ONDS Diehl Defence: System-of-Systems Overlap There is no direct standalone commercial treaty between Ondas and Diehl Defence, but they share an operational ecosystem: • Primes and Suppliers: Diehl Defence and Hensoldt heavily co-develop major software-defined ground air defenses (such as the IRIS-T SLM series). • Because Ondas acts as an orchestration and C-UAS software supplier for Hensoldt, Ondas’ sub-systems (like Sentrycs or the newly deployed LADOS defense orchestration layer) indirectly feed into the larger multi-layered network architectures that Diehl vehicles and missile clusters deploy alongside.

Sentrycs’ software-defined, open-architecture Cyber-over-RF C-UAS technology is actively integrated as a non-kinetic, soft-kill layer within Hensoldt’s broader multi-layer defense platform. • The ONBERG Ecosystem: Ondas' European joint venture, ONBERG, operates as a critical supplier and systems integrator in Germany. Major tier-1 primes like Hensoldt route complex multi-domain drone orchestration through ONBERG components before passing final assembly onto downstream military programs

items.title: OpenAI - $AMD (announced Oct 2025): OpenAI commits to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs (starting w/ the MI450 series in 2H26), across
items.content_excerpt: OpenAI - $AMD (announced Oct 2025): OpenAI commits to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs (starting w/ the MI450 series in 2H26), across multiple gens. AMD expects tens of billions in revs from this (w/ broader related rev projections exceeding $100B over time from the deal & its ripple effects). As part of aligning incentives, AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160M AMD shares (roughly 10% of the company at the time) exercisable at $0.01 per share • $META – AMD (announced Feb 2026): Nearly identical structure. Meta agrees to buy chips supporting up to 6 GW of AI compute (custom versions of the MI450 series & related CPUs, focused in part on inference), w/ 1st shipments of ~1 GW starting in 2H26. Reported deal value ests range from $60B to $100B+; each gigawatt is described as worth “double-digit billions” or tens of billions in revs for AMD. Meta receives a matching warrant for up to 160M shares at $0.01 Combined, full vesting would allow OpenAI + Meta to acquire up to ~320M shares (~20% of AMD) Vesting occurs in tranches tied to: • Actual chip deployments/purchases (1st tranche w/ the initial ~1 GW shipment; further tranches as volume scales toward 6 GW) • AMD stock-price targets (escalating, w/ the final tranche requiring AMD shares to reach $600) —- At the current ~$634 share price, the intrinsic value of the fully vested warrants would be enormous—roughly $101B–$102B for each of OpenAI & Meta (or ~$203B combined)

items.content_excerpt: $MSFT Wells Fargo raised its Microsoft target to 725 from 700 Thursday and added the stock to its Q4 Tactical Ideas list. About 40 percent upside from Friday's 517.53 close. The interesting part isn't the 25-point raise. Turrin's call leans on something mechanical: starting with fiscal Q1 results on October 27, Microsoft moves to two reporting segments (Agents and Infra, Devices and Consumer) and discloses Azure revenue separately. His read: cleaner disclosure gives more room for upside if Azure comes in hot. The FQ1 guide is 45 percent Azure growth in constant currency. Context: MSFT is up 37.5 percent in Q3, its best quarter since 1998, adding about a trillion in market cap after July's print showed Azure at 43 percent, the fastest cloud growth in four years.

items.title: OpenAI - $AMD (announced Oct 2025): OpenAI commits to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs (starting w/ the MI450 series in 2H26), across
items.content_excerpt: OpenAI - $AMD (announced Oct 2025): OpenAI commits to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs (starting w/ the MI450 series in 2H26), across multiple gens. AMD expects tens of billions in revs from this (w/ broader related rev projections exceeding $100B over time from the deal & its ripple effects). As part of aligning incentives, AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160M AMD shares (roughly 10% of the company at the time) exercisable at $0.01 per share • $META – AMD (announced Feb 2026): Nearly identical structure. Meta agrees to buy chips supporting up to 6 GW of AI compute (custom versions of the MI450 series & related CPUs, focused in part on inference), w/ 1st shipments of ~1 GW starting in 2H26. Reported deal value ests range from $60B to $100B+; each gigawatt is described as worth “double-digit billions” or tens of billions in revs for AMD. Meta receives a matching warrant for up to 160M shares at $0.01 Combined, full vesting would allow OpenAI + Meta to acquire up to ~320M shares (~20% of AMD) Vesting occurs in tranches tied to: • Actual chip deployments/purchases (1st tranche w/ the initial ~1 GW shipment; further tranches as volume scales toward 6 GW) • AMD stock-price targets (escalating, w/ the final tranche requiring AMD shares to reach $600) —- At the current ~$634 share price, the intrinsic value of the fully vested warrants would be enormous—roughly $101B–$102B for each of OpenAI & Meta (or ~$203B combined)

items.title: $META The problem with Muse is permissions as a one-app solution. Unless you are developing the actual software/OS (Windows, Mac, Google), t
items.content_excerpt: $META The problem with Muse is permissions as a one-app solution. Unless you are developing the actual software/OS (Windows, Mac, Google), there's going to be too much pushback from each outfit. Right now the big deal is the agent accessing full disk access and performing unwanted tasks. This security/privacy angle is going to be what Microsoft or Google latch on to in order to push their own products IMO. Plus no corporation is going to let their employees use Muse. They already block Facebook and IG etc. Maybe good as a layman's AI agent, but also the same consumer where things like this can be even more damaging since they're not familiar with app permissions or how to use their phone on a good day

As part of these discussions, Netlist shared with Micron presentations and details about Netlist’s patent portfolio, including patents and patent applications regarding 3D-stacked DRAM packages, of which HBM is an example. One of the patents Netlist disclosed to Micron in 2015 was USPatentNo 8,787,060—titled...—which is the parent for both Asserted Patents. Netlist eventually proposed entering into a strategic partnership with Micron, which would have included Netlist licensing its patent portfolio to Micron. Micron declined." "Feb 2011 Netlist gave a presentation to Elpida Memory, a Japanese memory manufacturer. The presentation, titled...disclosed...products, of which HBM products are examples. In 2012, Micron purchased Elpida. Rather than license Netlist’s patents, Micron chose to develop and manufacture its own HBM products that infringe Netlist’s patents."

items.content_excerpt: $BE Something I think the market may underestimate: time-to-power is becoming a product itself. Bloom recently introduced Power Connect, a standardized deployment system designed to move critical electrical integration from the field into the factory. Bloom says this can reduce onsite installation time by 40%+. When data centers and other power-intensive facilities are racing to secure electricity, shaving months—or even weeks—off deployment can have significant economic value. Bloom isn’t just selling power generation. It’s increasingly selling speed, reliability, and certainty of deployment. That could become a meaningful competitive advantage as the global race for electricity accelerates. $SPY $QQQ

items.title: $BE One thing I find particularly interesting about Bloom’s board is the network of experience behind it. Jim Snabe — Chairman of Siemens, f
items.content_excerpt: $BE One thing I find particularly interesting about Bloom’s board is the network of experience behind it. Jim Snabe — Chairman of Siemens, former SAP co-CEO, former Maersk chairman, and Temasek board member. Jeff Immelt — former GE Chairman & CEO, with decades of experience in global power markets and Fortune 500 customers. Barbara Burger — former Chevron VP of Innovation and President of Chevron Technology Ventures, with deep experience commercializing energy technologies. That’s a pretty unique combination of industrial power + global technology + energy expertise sitting around the table. For a company trying to scale rapidly into AI/data centers and global power markets, those connections could be extremely valuable. Not a reason by itself to buy $BE — but definitely something I’d want to see in a company I’m investing in. $SPY $QQQ $CVX

items.content_excerpt: $ARCT Time to panic? Residents of Russia's Irkutsk region are deeply worried by rumours of a possible outbreak of pneumonic plague in this Siberian area. Speculation began to spread rapidly after the death of an employee of the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute. Darya Shipilova died in the early hours of 2 October in the intensive care unit of the district hospital in the town of Shelekhov. According to local media, she broke a test tube containing the plague pathogen. The incident prompted authorities to introduce quarantine measures: around 200 people have been placed under strict medical observation. The outlet "Baikal People" (source in Russian) reports that several Irkutsk hospitals were immediately closed and placed under quarantine, due to last three weeks. On Saturday, masks were made compulsory as a preventive measure at the Irkutsk aluminium plant in Shelekhov. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/04/has-plague-returned-to-siberia-panic-in-russia-after-death-of-lab-worker

items.title: $HELP Grok details it: "The Q4 2026 APPROACH topline is built around one primary and one key secondary, both MADRS change from baseline
items.content_excerpt: $HELP Grok details it: "The Q4 2026 APPROACH topline is built around one primary and one key secondary, both MADRS change from baseline versus placebo. EMBRACE uses the same hierarchy. Helus has said the readout will include both timepoints plus safety. Primary — 6 weeks (day 42) Change from baseline in MADRS total score at day 42, versus placebo. Day 42 is six weeks after the first dose and three weeks after the second. This is the registrational efficacy test for APPROACH and for EMBRACE. Key secondary — 12 weeks (day 84) Same measure: change from baseline in MADRS total score at day 84, versus placebo. Company materials and the CMO frame this as the durability readout, not a second independent efficacy claim. Company IR slides label it “key secondary endpoint: MADRS change from baseline at 12 weeks.”" https://grok.com/share/c2hhcmQtMw_b84b3396-2563-48ce-9002-770f28c859d6

items.title: $STX $WDC Bernstein says Toshiba comments misunderstood, buy Seagate and Western Digital Bernstein believes Toshiba's comments yesterday
items.content_excerpt: $STX $WDC Bernstein says Toshiba comments misunderstood, buy Seagate and Western Digital Bernstein believes Toshiba's comments yesterday to double hard disk drive capacity were misunderstood. Toshiba's press release actually said that it is aiming to nearly double production capacity by fiscal 2027, which ends March 2028, the analyst tells investors in a research note. If Toshiba doubles exabyte output while Western Digital (WDC) and Seagate (STX) each grow exabyte by 25%, in line with their long-term plans, the resulting Toshiba exabyte share would increase from 11.2% to 16.8%, says Bernstein. The firm adds, "Although significant, a 5.6% increase in market share isn't that alarming and nowhere near the 30% market share reported in the press today." As such, Bernstein views yesterday's news as a "storm in a teacup" and would look to buy shares of Seagate and Western Digital on the selloff. It reiterates Outperform ratings on both names.

items.title: $PFE Pfizer presented Phase 3 vitiligo data for LITFULO yesterday at EADV in Vienna: two trials, 2,174 patients, which Pfizer says is the la
items.content_excerpt: $PFE Pfizer presented Phase 3 vitiligo data for LITFULO yesterday at EADV in Vienna: two trials, 2,174 patients, which Pfizer says is the largest oral systemic program in nonsegmental vitiligo to date. At the 100 mg dose, 21.86% of patients hit F-VASI75 at week 52 vs 2.40% on placebo. Total-body T-VASI50 was 13.02% vs 2.40%. The 50 mg dose came in at roughly half the effect. Benefit showed up by week 24 and kept growing through week 52. One level down: Incyte's Opzelura is the only FDA-approved vitiligo treatment, and it is a topical cream limited to 10% of body surface area. A once-daily oral has no coverage ceiling. But the oral race already has two horses. AbbVie's Rinvoq just won EU approval for vitiligo and is under FDA review. Safety read clean against placebo: serious adverse events 3.4% in both arms of the larger trial. Filings to FDA and EMA are the next catalyst.

items.title: $FRVO the ~10 days surrounding the lockup look like the highest-probability window for a final capitulation low. Bottom line: I put only abo
items.content_excerpt: $FRVO the ~10 days surrounding the lockup look like the highest-probability window for a final capitulation low. Bottom line: I put only about 25% odds that $13.44 is definitively the bottom, roughly 67% odds that the ultimate bottom is $9.50–$13, and my best estimate is ~$12.25, probably occurring around the lockup window. The last major pre-IPO Fervo investors (Series E-1) effectively paid about $11.36 per current FRVO share. The round immediately before Series E-1 was the December 2024 Series D-3. Investors paid $5.28 per pre-split share. With the 0.7194 conversion ratio, that’s equivalent to: $5.28 ÷ 0.7194 = ~$7.34 per current FRVO share. The round before the December 2024 Series D-3 was the February 2024 Series D-1. Investors paid $2.5323 per pre-split share. Fervo’s preferred shares converted into 0.7194 current FRVO shares, so: $2.5323 ÷ 0.7194 = ~$3.52 per current FRVO share. ~$3.52 → Series D-3 (Dec 2024): ~$7.34 → Series E-1 (Dec 2025): ~$11.36 → IPO: $27.00

$ONDS Diehl Defence: System-of-Systems Overlap There is no direct standalone commercial treaty between Ondas and Diehl Defence, but they share an operational ecosystem: • Primes and Suppliers: Diehl Defence and Hensoldt heavily co-develop major software-defined ground air defenses (such as the IRIS-T SLM series). • Because Ondas acts as an orchestration and C-UAS software supplier for Hensoldt, Ondas’ sub-systems (like Sentrycs or the newly deployed LADOS defense orchestration layer) indirectly feed into the larger multi-layered network architectures that Diehl vehicles and missile clusters deploy alongside.

$ONDS AI ---Hensoldt: Confirmed Integration & MOU Partner Ondas operates indirectly with Hensoldt through its core business layers: • The Sentrycs Architecture: Ondas' subsidiary, Sentrycs, has a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Hensoldt. Sentrycs’ software-defined, open-architecture Cyber-over-RF C-UAS technology is actively integrated as a non-kinetic, soft-kill layer within Hensoldt’s broader multi-layer defense platform. • The ONBERG Ecosystem: Ondas' European joint venture, ONBERG, operates as a critical supplier and systems integrator in Germany. Major tier-1 primes like Hensoldt route complex multi-domain drone orchestration through ONBERG components before passing final assembly onto downstream military programs

Is the current AI boom repeating the 2000 dot-com bubble again? $SPY $AAPL $TSLA $NVDA $MSFT There are genuine similarities such ad market leadership concentration, speculative enthusiasm. However, the key differences are far more significant. Valuations are nowhere near dot-com extremes, with the Nasdaq-100 trading around 26x forward earnings versus roughly 60x in 2000. More importantly, today's market leaders are extraordinarily profitable, generating tens of billions in cash flow and funding AI investments from their own operations rather than issuing stock to finance growth. Demand for AI infrastructure is also real and immediate, with cloud capacity, advanced chips, and foundry production largely sold out. A Nasdaq-style 78% crash remains a low-probability outcome without a severe economic shock.

Helus has said the readout will include both timepoints plus safety. Primary — 6 weeks (day 42) Change from baseline in MADRS total score at day 42, versus placebo. $PFE Pfizer presented Phase 3 vitiligo data for LITFULO yesterday at EADV in Vienna: two trials, 2,174 patients, which Pfizer says is the largest oral systemic program in nonsegmental vitiligo to date. At the 100 mg dose, 21.86% of patients hit F-VASI75 at week 52 vs 2.40% on placebo. Total-body T-VASI50 was 13.02% vs 2.40%. The 50 mg dose came in at roughly half the effect. Benefit showed up by week 24 and kept growing through week 52. One level down: Incyte's Opzelura is the only FDA-approved vitiligo treatment, and it is a topical cream limited to 10% of body surface area. A once-daily oral has no coverage ceiling. But the oral race already has two horses. AbbVie's Rinvoq just won EU approval for vitiligo and is under FDA review. Safety read clean against placebo: serious adverse events 3.4% in both arms of the larger trial. Filings to FDA and EMA are the next catalyst.
